overview: Docebo is a Toronto-based cloud SaaS company that provides an AI-powered enterprise learning and workforce readiness platform, dual-listed on NASDAQ and TSX. The company has evolved from a pure-play LMS into a multi-product platform that unifies skills intelligence (via the 365Talents acquisition), enterprise knowledge management (via the Zive acquisition), learning delivery, and agentic AI in a single closed loop. Docebo serves thousands of enterprise, mid-market, and public sector customers worldwide, generating over 90% of revenue from recurring subscriptions, with ARR of $255.1 million as of Q2 2026 (+9.5% YoY, or ~13.9% ex-OEM/ex-FX) — a second consecutive quarter of ARR growth re-acceleration.

business_model.summary: Subscription-based SaaS model with ~93% recurring subscription revenue and ~7% professional services. Multi-year contracts with annual renewals provide strong revenue visibility. The company is transitioning from a single-product LMS to a multi-product AI workforce readiness platform spanning learning, skills intelligence, and enterprise knowledge, and is now pushing into new verticals (healthcare) alongside its established government/FedRAMP push.

revenue_streams.name: Subscription Revenue
revenue_streams.description: Cloud-based platform with annual or multi-year contracts. Includes core LMS, OEM/extended enterprise, and increasingly 365Talents skills intelligence. Q2 2026: $63.8M, up 12% YoY. FY2026 guided to $255.5-257.5M.

revenue_streams.name: Professional Services
revenue_streams.description: Implementation, onboarding, project management, and integration services. Q2 2026: $4.8M, up 31% YoY, continuing the elevated growth seen since the Q1 2026 365Talents-driven spike.

business_model.customer_type: Enterprise (primary focus), mid-market, and public sector. Serves both Employee Experience (EX - internal training, compliance, onboarding) and Customer/Partner Experience (CX - external academies, channel enablement). Also serves OEM partners who embed Docebo into their own software products. New vertical push into healthcare (~$10M existing ARR base, targeting a ~$3B TAM) launched in Q2 2026, modeled on the government vertical playbook.
business_model.geographic_mix: North America dominant, with international (particularly Europe, aided by 365Talents/Zive footholds) growing faster than North America. Historically ~29% Rest of World as of Q1 2026; management continues to cite international and FX as tailwinds to reported growth.
business_model.pricing_model: Per-learner or per-user subscription with tiered plans. Average Contract Value (ACV) reached $74,800 as of Q2 2026, up 27% YoY from ~$58,900 in Q2 2025 — the fastest ACV growth rate reported to date, continuing acceleration from Q1 2026's 25.9% growth. Reflects enterprise upmarket shift, 365Talents cross-sell, and price increases on renewal.
business_model.go_to_market: Direct enterprise sales force for large accounts, systems integrator partnerships (Deloitte, NIIT, and others) for government and complex deals, inside sales for mid-market. Roughly 80% of enterprise deals now involve a partner. Growing partner channel and OEM channel. Land-and-expand strategy to grow ACV within existing customers through upsells (AI features, new products) and expanded use cases. New standalone go-to-market motion being staffed for the healthcare vertical (dedicated sales leadership and engineering).

main_competitors: Cornerstone OnDemand (enterprise leader, largest market share)
SAP SuccessFactors Learning / SAP Litmos (enterprise HCM suite)
Workday Learning (bundled in Workday HCM suite)
LinkedIn Learning / Microsoft Viva Learning (bundled in Microsoft 365)
competitive_position.market_position: Positioned as a fast-growing challenger in the enterprise LMS market, targeting the intersection of learning, skills intelligence, and agentic AI. Strong in mid-enterprise and growing in large enterprise and government (FedRAMP certified). Q2 2026 marked a second consecutive quarter of ARR re-acceleration with management describing broad-based strength across net-new, expansion, and international. ACV of $74.8K and 27% YoY growth signals continued and accelerating upmarket movement. New healthcare vertical entry (competitive displacement win in Philadelphia behavioral health market) signals confidence in replicating the FedRAMP-style vertical playbook.

moat_factors.description: The combination of Docebo LMS, 365Talents skills intelligence, Zive enterprise knowledge, and AgentHub creates a closed-loop AI workforce readiness platform that few competitors can match end-to-end. Management says 365Talents integration is 'ahead of schedule' six months post-close and has directly enabled marquee wins (world's largest telecom/networking company, world's largest automotive safety systems supplier) that management says would not have closed without the 365Talents capability.

Docebo AgentHub and Enterprise Knowledge are now guided to general availability in early Fall 2026 (in line with prior 'Fall 2026' plan). Management describes work underway on custom agent workflows for vertical use cases (QSR, healthcare, financial services), but has not yet disclosed adoption metrics, pilot counts, or confirmed a completed MCP Server GA (originally targeted for July 2026) — this could not be independently confirmed as reached in disclosed Q2 materials and should be treated as unconfirmed pending the next update.

Unique ability to serve both internal (EX) and external (CX - customers, partners, franchisees) learning on one platform. OEM channel embeds Docebo into other software products. Demonstrated in wins with global QSR chains, tech companies, and now a world's-largest private security services firm (130K workforce) and a global telecom leader.

FedRAMP Moderate Authorization (achieved 2025) continues to unlock the U.S. federal and SLED market. Q2 2026 government revenue was described as a 'record flat quarter' with new wins including Commonwealth of Kentucky enterprise learning modernization, Indiana Public Retirement System, State of Mississippi, and — notably — a private-sector energy company win explicitly attributed to FedRAMP-grade security credibility (i.e., the FedRAMP moat is starting to help win non-government deals too). Management flagged Q3 2026 as a 'heavy federal quarter' with material pipeline, though specifics were not disclosed.

LMS data, integrations, custom branding, content libraries, and now cross-product tie-ins (skills + learning) create meaningful migration friction. Multi-product adoption (365Talents cross-sell) raises switching costs further. FY2025 NDRR was 99%; a specific Q2 2026 NDRR figure was not disclosed in the sources reviewed for this refresh and should be confirmed from the full MD&A/financial statements.

Recognized for rapid AI innovation cycles. Strong NPS and customer references, including several 'world's largest' logos closed in Q2 2026. Less brand recognition in large enterprise versus SAP or Cornerstone.

competitive_position.differentiation: Primary differentiation through: (1) unified AI workforce readiness platform (LMS + skills + knowledge + agents in one loop), (2) dual CX/EX capabilities with OEM channel, (3) agentic AI and open ecosystem ambitions (AgentHub GA targeted early Fall 2026), (4) FedRAMP-certified for government market and now leveraging that credibility into commercial energy-sector wins, and (5) a repeatable vertical-expansion playbook now being applied to healthcare.
weaknesses: Smaller scale and resources versus SAP, Workday, Microsoft which bundle LMS in suite at no incremental cost
Net Dollar Retention was 99% in FY2025 (below best-in-class SaaS benchmarks); no update disclosed for Q2 2026 in sources reviewed
OEM customer concentration continuing to decline (largest OEM customer down to 2.5% of ARR from 8.4% YoY as of Q2 2026) — a shrinking headwind but still a mix/comp distortion on headline ARR growth
Gross margin continued to compress: 79.4% in Q2 2026 vs 80.9% in Q2 2025, reflecting 365Talents/Zive mix and AI service costs
GAAP profitability is thin and volatile: Q2 2026 GAAP net income was only $2.3M ($0.09/share) despite $11.2M Adjusted EBITDA

Operating cash flow was reported negative in Q2 2026 (-$3.1M) even as free cash flow was reported positive ($3.1M) — this OCF/FCF divergence is unusual and should be reconciled against the full financial statements before being relied upon in a DCF
Balance sheet leverage has increased further, not stabilized (see Corporate Actions below)

growth_drivers.driver: Multi-Product Platform Expansion (365Talents + Zive) — Ahead of Schedule
growth_drivers.description: Management explicitly stated on the Q2 2026 call that 365Talents integration is 'ahead of schedule' six months post-acquisition, with pipeline targets described as 'blown up' (exceeded). Cited marquee wins directly attributable to 365Talents capability: the world's largest telecom/networking company and the world's largest automotive safety systems supplier. This is a positive, more concrete confirmation of the cross-sell thesis than existed at the June 2026 checkpoint.

Docebo AgentHub and Enterprise Knowledge are guided for general availability in early Fall 2026, consistent with the prior 'Fall 2026' target. Custom agent workflows for vertical use cases (QSR, healthcare, financial services) are in development. MCP Server's originally-targeted July 2026 GA was not explicitly confirmed as reached in Q2 2026 disclosures reviewed — this is a gap to close in the next earnings cycle, not a confirmed milestone.

growth_drivers.driver: Government and Public Sector (FedRAMP) — Now Bleeding into Commercial
growth_drivers.description: FedRAMP Moderate Authorization continues to generate SLED wins (Kentucky, Indiana, Mississippi in Q2 2026 alone) and, notably, its first flagged commercial win explicitly attributed to FedRAMP-grade security credibility (a private-sector energy company). Management flagged Q3 2026 as a 'heavy federal quarter.' Government revenue was described as a 'record flat quarter' in Q2 2026 (terminology suggesting a quarter without the typical seasonal dip, though exact dollar figures were not disclosed in sources reviewed).

Docebo is entering healthcare as a discrete strategic vertical, sized at ~$3B TAM within the broader ~$30B corporate learning market, leveraging an existing ~$10M ARR healthcare base. Management is replicating the government-vertical playbook: dedicated sales leadership and engineering investment, with an initial competitive displacement win in the Philadelphia behavioral health market. Management's own framing is 'months rather than years' to build competitive capability — a new, not-previously-modeled growth avenue as of the June 2026 analysis.

ACV reached $74,800 in Q2 2026, +27% YoY, up from +25.9% YoY in Q1 2026 — acceleration, not deceleration. Reflects successful upmarket shift, continued 365Talents cross-selling, and new large-logo wins (global telecom leader, 130K-workforce security firm, automotive safety leader, top global consulting firm).

Q2 2026 marked the second consecutive quarter of ARR growth re-acceleration (Q1 2026: +10.6% reported/+13.7% ex-OEM/ex-FX; Q2 2026: +9.5% reported/~13.9% ex-OEM/ex-FX), with management describing the strength as broad-based across net-new, expansion, and international segments — a positive continuation and slight strengthening of the trend flagged as a bull case in the June 2026 analysis.

International growth remains a stated driver, aided by 365Talents (France) and Zive (Germany) footholds in continental Europe and continued FX tailwind from a weaker USD. No updated regional revenue split was disclosed in sources reviewed for this refresh.
Global corporate e-learning/LMS market growth and the AI-driven platform replacement cycle remain the long-term secular backdrop; unchanged from the prior analysis.

growth_drivers.driver: Shareholder Returns - Buybacks (Now a Second, Larger SIB)
growth_drivers.description: Following the $60M SIB completed March 2026, Docebo launched a SECOND, larger Substantial Issuer Bid on July 17, 2026: up to US$70M (3.43M shares, ~13.8% of shares outstanding on a non-diluted basis) at US$20.40/share, running July 21-August 26, 2026. This is funded by ~$10M cash and a $60M draw on a credit facility that was simultaneously expanded from $100M to $150M. Major shareholder Intercap Inc. (~63.9% ownership) intends to participate pro-rata to maintain its ownership percentage. Management again stated the stock price is 'not fully reflective' of business value. This is a materially larger and more leveraged capital return than what existed at the June 2026 checkpoint and should be flagged prominently — see Corporate Actions.

business.description: Largest OEM customer declined further to 2.5% of ARR in Q2 2026 (from 8.4% a year prior, and from 3.2% at Q1 2026 on the prior comparable-period basis). The unwind appears to be nearly complete and is now a smaller drag on headline growth than in 2025, reducing this risk's severity versus the June 2026 assessment.

Large enterprise deals remain a swing factor for guidance beats/misses. Q2 2026 total revenue beat consensus, but subscription revenue reportedly came in slightly below some analyst estimates even as total revenue beat — a reminder that mix (services vs. subscription) can create noisy quarter-to-quarter comparisons.

SAP SuccessFactors, Workday, and Microsoft (Viva Learning bundled in M365) continue to compete for LMS budget via broader HCM suites. No material new competitive moves from these vendors were identified in this refresh window, but the underlying risk is unchanged.

FY2025 NDRR was 99%. A specific, confirmed Q2 2026 NDRR figure could not be located in the sources reviewed for this refresh (searches returned only the FY2025 figure). This is a gap that should be closed from the full financial statements/MD&A before treating NDRR as unchanged or improved.

The healthcare vertical push is new since the June 2026 analysis: management is committing to build out dedicated sales and engineering capability from a small (~$10M ARR) existing base, targeting rapid ('months not years') competitive parity. This is an additional execution front layered on top of the already-ambitious 365Talents/Zive/AgentHub integration roadmap, increasing overall organizational execution risk even as it expands TAM.

financial.risk: Leverage Has Increased Further, Not Stabilized
financial.description: As of Q2 2026: cash of $45.7M (down sharply from $74.0M at FY2025 year-end) against total debt of $88.0M. The credit facility was expanded from $100M to $150M specifically to fund a SECOND $70M buyback (on top of the March 2026 $60M SIB), with a further $60M draw planned/underway. This is a clear escalation in balance-sheet leverage versus the June 2026 analysis, which was already flagging near-zero/negative shareholders' equity. Severity raised from 'moderate' to 'high' this refresh given the deliberate, repeated choice to lever up further for buybacks rather than delever after the acquisitions.

financial.risk: Free Cash Flow Deceleration / OCF-FCF Divergence
financial.description: Q2 2026 free cash flow was reported at just $3.1M (4.5% of revenue), a sharp decline from the ~18-19% FCF margin reported a year earlier, while operating cash flow was reported NEGATIVE (-$3.1M) in the same quarter. This combination is unusual (FCF exceeding OCF implies either a working-capital-driven distortion, non-standard FCF definition, or a data inconsistency across sources) and could not be fully reconciled from the secondary sources reviewed. This needs verification directly against Docebo's reported cash flow statement before being used as a DCF input — if accurate, it materially undercuts the 'strong FCF generation' framing used as a bull point in the prior analysis.

365Talents integration is reported by management as ahead of schedule with concrete customer-win evidence, somewhat reducing this risk versus June 2026. Zive/Enterprise Knowledge and AgentHub remain pre-GA (targeted early Fall 2026) and unproven at scale.

Gross margin fell further to 79.4% in Q2 2026 from 80.9% a year earlier, continuing the trend flagged in the June 2026 analysis (81% FY2024 to 80.3% FY2025 to 78.1% Q1 2026 to 79.4% Q2 2026 — roughly stable sequentially but still down YoY).
Unchanged from prior analysis; USD weakness continues to provide a reported-growth tailwind that could reverse.

regulatory.risk: EU AI Act and Emerging AI Governance

regulatory.description: Unchanged from prior analysis; FedRAMP credibility is now beginning to help win non-government (energy sector) commercial deals, a modest positive development.

execution.risk: Multi-Front Execution Load Has Grown, Not Shrunk
execution.description: In addition to integrating 365Talents and Zive and launching AgentHub/Enterprise Knowledge, Docebo is now simultaneously: (1) running a second, larger, more leveraged buyback program, (2) standing up a new healthcare vertical from scratch, and (3) preparing for a 'heavy federal quarter' pipeline push in Q3 2026. The number of concurrent strategic initiatives at a company of Docebo's scale (~$255M ARR) has increased since the June 2026 analysis, not decreased.

Launching a second debt-funded buyback within approximately four months of completing the first (and while still digesting two acquisitions) raises a legitimate question of capital allocation sequencing versus balance-sheet repair. CFO commentary indicated the new SIB, priced at the same $20.40 as the March SIB, may see limited tendering given the stock was trading close to that level ($18.54 pre-announcement) — meaning the buyback's realized impact may differ from its headline $70M size.

No new management changes were identified in Q2 2026 sources reviewed. CEO Artuffo and CFO Farber led the Q2 2026 call; the leadership team appears to remain stable, an improvement in certainty versus the turnover flagged in 2024-2025.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global LMS and corporate e-learning market outlook is unchanged from the prior analysis: continued growth driven by digital transformation, compliance mandates, and the skills-based organization trend, with AI-native platforms increasingly displacing legacy LMS incumbents.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate cyclicality; unchanged from prior analysis.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate-to-higher direct sensitivity than previously assessed: total debt has grown to $88.0M as of Q2 2026 and is set to increase further with the pending $60M draw for the new SIB (against an expanded $150M facility), raising direct interest-rate sensitivity versus the June 2026 analysis (which cited an $80M facility).
key_input_costs: Cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, Azure) for platform hosting
Third-party AI API services (OpenAI, Google, AWS AI) - growing cost as AI features expand
R&D engineering talent (competitive market for AI/ML engineers in Toronto, Italy, France, and now healthcare-vertical specialists)
Sales and marketing (customer acquisition cost, SI partnership development, new healthcare vertical build-out costs)
macro_factors.regulatory_environment: Unchanged from prior analysis; FedRAMP continues to be a net positive differentiator, now also assisting commercial (non-government) sales.

recent_developments.event: Q2 2026 Final Results Reported - Revenue Beat, ARR Re-Acceleration Continues, Guidance Raised Again
recent_developments.impact: Docebo reported final (non-preliminary) Q2 2026 results: total revenue $68.7M (+13% YoY), subscription revenue $63.8M (+12% YoY), professional services $4.8M (+31% YoY), ARR $255.1M (+9.5% YoY, ~13.9% ex-OEM/ex-FX), ACV $74,800 (+27% YoY, an acceleration from Q1's +25.9%), gross margin 79.4% (down from 80.9% YoY), Adjusted EBITDA $11.2M (16.4% margin), Adjusted EPS $0.35 (beat consensus ~$0.30), GAAP net income $2.3M ($0.09/share), Adjusted net income $9.4M ($0.37/share). Free cash flow reported at $3.1M (4.5% of revenue) alongside a reported NEGATIVE operating cash flow of $(3.1)M -- an unusual divergence flagged for further verification. Cash fell to $45.7M (from $74.0M at FY2025 year-end) and total debt stood at $88.0M. FY2026 guidance raised to total revenue $274.5-276.5M / subscription revenue $255.5-257.5M / Adjusted EBITDA $54.5-56.5M (up from the Q1-raised $271-273M / $253.5-255.5M / $54.5-56.5M -- note the EBITDA guidance range midpoint was maintained rather than raised, while revenue guidance moved up further). Initial Q3 2026 guidance: total revenue $69.5-69.7M, subscription revenue $64.9-65.1M, Adjusted EBITDA $15.9-16.1M (implying a large sequential EBITDA margin step-up to ~23%). Stock reaction was muted (roughly flat to slightly down intraday), and several sell-side analysts CUT price targets afterward (average consensus target reportedly fell to roughly C$26 from roughly C$31) despite the headline beat-and-raise, suggesting the market/analysts focused on the FCF softness and/or the newly announced leverage rather than the top-line beat.

recent_developments.event: Second Substantial Issuer Bid Announced - Up to US$70M, Funded Mostly by New Debt; Credit Facility Expanded to $150M
recent_developments.impact: Docebo announced a second SIB (following the $60M SIB completed March 2026) to repurchase up to 3,431,372 common shares (~13.8% of shares outstanding on a non-diluted basis) at US$20.40/share, for an aggregate of up to US$70M. The offer commenced July 21, 2026 and is scheduled to expire August 26, 2026 (i.e., is LIVE/ongoing as of this refresh date), with no minimum tender condition. Funding: ~US$10M cash plus a US$60M draw on the company's credit facility, which was simultaneously expanded from US$100M to US$150M. Major shareholder Intercap Inc. (~63.9% of shares) intends to participate pro-rata to maintain its ownership percentage. Management again characterized the stock as undervalued. This was announced alongside preliminary (subsequently finalized on Aug 7) Q2 2026 results and initial Q3 2026 / revised FY2026 guidance. This is a materially significant corporate action: it further increases leverage (total debt approaching/exceeding $148M pro forma for the full draw against $45.7M cash) only ~4 months after the prior debt-funded SIB and while two acquisitions are still being integrated. FLAGGED AS A KEY VALUATION INPUT CHANGE for any DCF/balance-sheet-based re-research.

Docebo announced a formal strategic push into healthcare as a discrete vertical, sized at ~$3B TAM within a ~$30B total corporate learning market, leveraging an existing ~$10M ARR healthcare customer base. Management is replicating its government-vertical playbook (dedicated sales leadership plus engineering investment) and cited an initial competitive-displacement win in the Philadelphia behavioral health market. This is a new growth driver not present in the June 2026 analysis.

recent_developments.event: 365Talents Integration 'Ahead of Schedule'; Concrete Cross-Sell Wins Disclosed
recent_developments.impact: On the Q2 2026 earnings call, management described 365Talents integration (six months post-close) as ahead of schedule, with pipeline targets exceeded ('blown up'). Specific enterprise wins cited as directly attributable to the combined 365Talents/Docebo capability: the world's largest telecom/networking company and the world's largest automotive safety systems supplier. This provides more concrete evidence for the multi-product cross-sell thesis than existed at the June 2026 checkpoint.

recent_developments.event: FedRAMP Credibility Wins First Flagged Commercial (Non-Government) Deal
recent_developments.impact: Management disclosed a private-sector energy company win explicitly attributed to Docebo's FedRAMP-grade security posture, alongside continued public-sector/SLED wins (Commonwealth of Kentucky, Indiana Public Retirement System, State of Mississippi). Government revenue was described as a 'record flat quarter' and management flagged Q3 2026 as a 'heavy federal quarter' with material (but undisclosed) pipeline.

recent_developments.event: Docebo Inspire 2026 - AgentHub, Enterprise Knowledge, MCP Server Launch Plans Announced
recent_developments.impact: Docebo unveiled its next-generation AI workforce readiness platform at Inspire 2026: Docebo AgentHub (full launch guided to early Fall 2026, reaffirmed at Q2 2026), Docebo MCP Server (targeted GA July 2026 -- NOT explicitly confirmed as reached in Q2 2026 disclosures reviewed for this refresh; status should be treated as unconfirmed), Enterprise Knowledge, and Companion. ATB Capital raised its price target to C$36 following the announcements (subsequent to Q2 2026 results, several analysts including ATB's peers have instead CUT targets -- see August 2026 entry above).

recent_developments.event: Acquisition of Zive GmbH (AI Knowledge Platform, Germany)
recent_developments.impact: Acquired Zive GmbH for $7.2M cash plus up to $1.0M earn-out, underpinning the new Enterprise Knowledge product and MCP Server capabilities. Unchanged from prior analysis; no major new disclosures on Zive-specific traction identified in this refresh.

recent_developments.event: First Substantial Issuer Bid Completed - $60M Buyback at $20.40
recent_developments.impact: Completed $60M SIB repurchasing 2.94M shares at $20.40/share, financed partly through an $80M draw on the then-$100M NBC credit facility. This was the first of what is now TWO debt-funded buybacks in 2026 (see the July 2026 second SIB above).

recent_developments.event: Acquisition of 365Talents (AI Skills Intelligence, France) for $54.6M
recent_developments.impact: Unchanged from prior analysis. Now validated by concrete Q2 2026 cross-sell wins (see above) and management's 'ahead of schedule' characterization.

guidance.as_of: Q2 2026 Earnings (August 7, 2026; terms first previewed in preliminary release July 17, 2026)

items.notes: Raised from the Q1-set $271.0-273.0M guidance. Implies roughly 13-14% YoY growth (FY2025: $242.7M). Raise attributed by management to a combination of Q2 beat flow-through (~$1.6M) plus incremental flow-through (~$2.1M), consistent with the ~$3.5M total guidance raise reported.
Raised from the Q1-set $253.5-255.5M. Implies roughly 12-13% YoY growth (FY2025: $228.4M).

Held at the same $54.5-56.5M range set at Q1 2026, even though revenue guidance was raised further -- implies a modest full-year Adjusted EBITDA margin guide-down in percentage terms relative to the higher revenue base, worth watching. Q3 2026 guidance of $15.9-16.1M implies a large sequential margin step-up to ~23% in Q3, so full-year margin delivery is now more back-half-weighted than at the Q1 checkpoint.
Initial Q3 2026 guidance, first given July 17, 2026 and reaffirmed August 7, 2026.
Implies ~23% Adjusted EBITDA margin, a large step-up from Q2 2026's 16.4% -- the primary driver of full-year margin achievement is now concentrated in Q3/Q4.
Unchanged assumption; integration now described by management as ahead of schedule with concrete cross-sell wins.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Alessio Artuffo stated Q2 2026 was 'another milestone quarter for Docebo as disciplined execution and long-term investment continued to strengthen our position with enterprise customers around the world,' and separately framed the shift toward 'enterprise-scale workforce transformation' as increasingly favoring Docebo. CFO Brandon Farber, discussing the new $70M SIB priced at the same $20.40 as the March SIB, noted that with the stock trading close to that level the company may see 'fairly [little] to frankly no shares tendered' -- an unusually candid signal that the buyback's realized size may fall well short of the headline $70M. Management reiterated buybacks as the 'top priority' for capital allocation. On the healthcare vertical, management set an internal expectation of improving win rates within 'months rather than years.' Q3 2026 was flagged as a 'heavy federal quarter.'

bull_case.point: ARR Re-Acceleration Now Confirmed for a Second Consecutive Quarter
bull_case.description: Q2 2026 marked the second straight quarter of ARR growth re-acceleration (Q1: +13.7% ex-OEM/ex-FX, Q2: ~13.9% ex-OEM/ex-FX), with management citing broad-based strength across net-new, expansion, and international. Combined with ACV accelerating to +27% YoY ($74.8K), the growth-reacceleration thesis flagged as speculative in June 2026 now has two data points of confirmation rather than one.

bull_case.point: 365Talents Cross-Sell Thesis Now Has Concrete Proof Points
bull_case.description: Management's 'ahead of schedule' characterization of the 365Talents integration is now backed by named marquee wins (world's largest telecom company, world's largest auto-safety supplier) explicitly attributed to the combined capability -- stronger evidence for the multi-product platform thesis than the largely aspirational framing available in June 2026.

bull_case.point: FedRAMP Credibility Is Starting to Sell Commercial Deals, Not Just Government Ones
bull_case.description: The private-sector energy company win attributed to FedRAMP-grade security marks the first evidence that the government-certification investment is generating a halo effect in commercial markets, potentially widening the addressable moat beyond the original SLED/federal thesis. Combined with a new healthcare vertical (targeting a $3B TAM from a $10M ARR base using the same playbook), Docebo is demonstrating a repeatable vertical-expansion model.

Docebo has now raised full-year revenue guidance in consecutive quarters (Q4 2025 initial guide, Q1 2026 raise, and again at Q2 2026), with Q2 2026 revenue beating consensus by roughly $1.8M and adjusted EPS beating by ~$0.05. This is a fourth consecutive quarter of guidance credibility being built.

bull_case.point: Management Conviction Signaled Through Repeated, Large Buybacks
bull_case.description: Two debt-funded SIBs within five months (totaling up to $130M) at prices management repeatedly calls undervalued, plus a controlling shareholder (Intercap, ~63.9%) participating pro-rata rather than cashing out, together signal strong insider conviction in intrinsic value versus the current quote.

bear_case.point: Balance Sheet Leverage Has Escalated, Not Stabilized -- This Is the Single Biggest Change Since June 2026
bear_case.description: Rather than deleveraging after digesting the March 2026 SIB and two acquisitions, Docebo announced a SECOND, larger ($70M) debt-funded SIB in July 2026, expanding its credit facility from $100M to $150M and drawing a further $60M. Cash fell from $74.0M (FY2025 year-end) to $45.7M (Q2 2026) while total debt stands at $88.0M and is set to rise further as the new SIB draw completes (offer runs through August 26, 2026). This is a material, adverse change to the capital structure underlying any DCF built on the June 2026 analysis and should be re-modeled with updated net debt.

bear_case.point: Free Cash Flow Weakened Sharply and Shows an Unexplained OCF/FCF Divergence
bear_case.description: Q2 2026 FCF margin fell to just 4.5% of revenue (from ~18-19% a year earlier) while operating cash flow was reported NEGATIVE ($(3.1)M) in the same quarter -- an internally inconsistent-looking combination across the sources reviewed that was not resolved by available secondary reporting. If accurate, this undercuts the 'strong, cash-generative SaaS business' framing central to the prior bull case and needs direct verification against the primary financial statements before use in any valuation model.

bear_case.point: Analysts Cut Price Targets Despite the Beat-and-Raise
bear_case.description: Despite total revenue beating consensus and FY2026 guidance being raised again, average analyst price targets reportedly fell to roughly C$26 from roughly C$31 following Q2 2026 results (though individual analyst targets remain widely dispersed, from National Bank's C$22 to TD's C$37), and the stock's own reaction was muted-to-slightly-negative. This suggests the market is weighing the FCF softness and rising leverage more heavily than the headline growth beat -- a signal worth taking seriously rather than dismissing as noise.

bear_case.point: Adjusted EBITDA Guidance Was Held Flat, Not Raised, Even as Revenue Guidance Rose Again
bear_case.description: FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance stayed at $54.5-56.5M even as total revenue guidance was raised to $274.5-276.5M, implying a slight full-year margin dilution versus the Q1 checkpoint. The heavy skew of margin delivery into Q3 2026 (guided to ~23% margin, up sharply from Q2's 16.4%) concentrates execution risk into a single quarter.

bear_case.point: Execution Load Has Grown Faster Than the Team Has Proven It Can Absorb
bear_case.description: On top of integrating 365Talents and Zive and launching AgentHub/Enterprise Knowledge, Docebo is now simultaneously running a second leveraged buyback, standing up a brand-new healthcare vertical from a small base, and preparing for a 'heavy' federal quarter -- a broader set of concurrent strategic bets than existed at the June 2026 checkpoint, at a company still only ~$275M in guided FY2026 revenue.

bear_case.point: NDRR Remains Unconfirmed and Potentially Stagnant
bear_case.description: FY2025 net dollar retention was 99%, and no updated Q2 2026 figure could be confirmed from the sources reviewed for this refresh. Until a current NDRR is disclosed, there is no direct evidence that cross-sell/expansion within the existing customer base has actually improved, despite management's qualitative claims about 365Talents cross-sell wins (which so far are described only via a handful of large new-logo examples, not a base-wide retention metric).
